questions.def: Use 'more' with longer adjectives for comparative forms.
questions.question: This book is ___ than the last one I read.

questions.def: 'As...as' is used to show equality in comparison.
questions.question: She is ___ as her brother.

questions.def: 'Best' is the superlative form of 'good'.
questions.question: This is the ___ day of my life!

questions.def: 'The more...the more' shows a proportional relationship.
questions.question: The ___ you practice, the better you become.

questions.def: 'As...as' is used for comparisons, often with a negative.
questions.question: He is not ___ intelligent as his sister.

questions.def: 'Worst' is the superlative form of 'bad'.
questions.question: This is the ___ movie I've ever seen.

questions.def: 'Less' indicates a smaller amount or degree.
questions.question: My car is ___ expensive than yours.

questions.def: 'More delicious' is used for comparing the degree of deliciousness.
questions.question: The food was ___ delicious than I expected.

questions.def: 'Farther' is the comparative form of 'far', referring to physical distance.
questions.question: London is ___ from here than Paris.

questions.def: 'Less' indicates a smaller degree of interest.
questions.question: She is ___ interested in sports than her sister.

questions.def: 'More difficult' is used for comparing the degree of difficulty.
questions.question: This exercise is ___ difficult than the last one.

questions.def: 'Easier' is the comparative form of 'easy'.

questions.def: 'The more...the more' shows a proportional relationship.

questions.def: 'As...as' is used for comparisons, often with a negative.

questions.def: 'Heavier' is the comparative form of 'heavy'.
questions.question: This box is ___ than the other one.

questions.def: 'More' is used with uncountable nouns like money.
questions.question: He has ___ money than I do.

questions.def: 'More quickly' for adverbs ending in -ly.
questions.question: She runs ___ quickly than her brother.

questions.def: 'Less' is used with uncountable nouns like time.

questions.def: 'Most' is used for superlatives with longer adjectives.
questions.question: This is the ___ popular restaurant in town.

questions.def: 'More beautifully' for adverbs ending in -ly.
questions.question: She sings ___ beautifully than her sister.

questions.def: 'Biggest' is the superlative form of 'big'.
questions.question: This is the ___ apple I've ever seen.

questions.def: 'The longer...the more' shows a proportional relationship.

questions.def: Use comparative form to show increasing degree.

questions.def: Parallel increase requires two comparatives.
